summary: For every ES word γ=[[cu−1,p],[c,cB−1]] (c=4C) the fixed form is [c, c(B−u), −p] of disc (a+d)²−4 = (c(u+B)−2)²−4, so p always sits on the river edge adjacent to the value c with edge label ≡0 mod c — a tautological location; computed all words/rivers for p<500 (no word at p=409 as expected), and the discriminant depends only on c(u+B), shared across many p. This is exactly the X-certificate ambiguous form [−t,tβ,p] of disc T²−4 in WINDMILL_REDUCTION §5.2/§8 (reduces to the e/t-slice problem) plus §10 Prop 10.3 (form-class mechanisms see only the genus shadow).

The fixed-C generating function Σ_{u,B≥1} q^{4CuB−u−B} is the degenerate (split, a=c=0) Hecke-type double sum; METAPLECTIC_ES Thm K (via Kronecker's double-series identity) already writes positive-cone minus partner-cone as the Kronecker theta quotient q^{t−2}(Q;Q)²θ(X²)/θ(X)² (odd-character divisor sums, holomorphic Jacobi-form data, no mock part) and the even part as even-character divisor sums. BRAINSTORM/z39_square_discriminant_shadow.md and z39_kronecker_levels.md record that no Appell–Lerch/mock part appears (Hickerson–Mortenson degenerate case); the 'two-sign' count N₋−N₊ is exactly D⁻−D⁺ of (K1′).

Setting up the first step shows the 𝔽_p formulation degenerates: every Type II certificate has ff′ = 1 + 4c²dp ≡ 1 (mod p), so all certificate points lie on the single curve xy = 1 in 𝔽_p² for every (c,d) — the (c,d)-family is only visible over ℤ, where the curves are hyperbolas xy = 1+4c²dp and Stevens–de Zeeuw/Rudnev (verified: arXiv:1609.06284) give only incidence UPPER bounds. That is exactly gon_incidence_kloosterman.md §3 (c2): incidence bounds bound f(p) from above, existence needs lower bounds that come only from identities (B1); a second-moment use only reproduces average-over-p results.

Computed the cheapest integer parity count, R(p)/2 = #unordered (★) triples mod 2, for the 147 primes p≡1 (4) < 2000: 75 odd / 72 even, and R=0 at 409, 577 — no parity law (matches WINDMILL_REDUCTION §3.3 '~50/50'). Chevalley–Warning/Ax–Katz count 𝔽_q-points, i.e. local data, which hold equally at odd squares (T1) — already recorded in B2_ACROSS_FIELDS §5 M5, BRAINSTORM/invol_topological.md (G-L/CW paragraph) and polynomial_method.md (b3: zero-sum methods certify +1, ES needs −1); no F₂-encoding of the integer certificate set was found that escapes this.

SINGLE_P_COUNT §6 Prop 6.1 (summary BRAINSTORM/z30_sl2_double_coset.md) already wrote R(p) as the count of −γ∈Γ₁(c) with b(γ)=p, c=4C its own lower-left entry: there is one Γ_∞-double coset per level c, and selecting the class a≡d≡−1 needs all frequencies mod c, so inside a coset b=p is just the divisor problem of cp+1; the transposed picture has a single level p with a height-dependent target. Neither yields Σ_c S(m,n;c) with fixed (m,n) over a long c-range, so Kuznetsov/Proskurin main terms enter only after averaging over p ((D)32, B6); the item's first step is exactly this computation.

Computed the image mod q of all length-3 ES words T^u(−1 0; c −1)T^B = [[cu−1,(cu−1)B−u],[c,cB−1]] (4|c when 4|q) in SL₂(ℤ/q) for q ≤ 40 and q ∈ {48,60,64,97,120}: for prime q it covers ≈ 1−1/q of SL₂ (all c invertible), with the 4|c restriction ≈ 5–8% (all matrices allowed by c ≡ 0 mod 4), and every unit b-entry (= p mod q) is hit for every q. So the short-word image mod q is already locally full with no expansion needed — the obstruction is integral (b = p exactly, entries in the word range), which is local-to-global data that Bourgain–Gamburd/Varjú (long-word equidistribution mod q) cannot see and which holds equally at odd squares (T1/B5).

Instead of a blind polynomial ansatz I tested the obstruction for identities in (a,b) with p = a²+b²: by Hilbert 90, N(α)=s² ⇔ α = s·δ²/N(δ), so locally every coset (a0,b0) mod M whose norm is a unit square mod M (exactly the Mordell-hard situation) contains odd-square-norm points; CERTIFIED by enumeration for M = 40 (128/128 cosets) and M = 120 (512/512) with m coprime to M. Hence a 2-variable identity valid on such a coset is evaluated at some a²+b² = m² and meets T1 (Type I/II at odd squares impossible), which is the 'two-variable Theorem M / square-mimicking point' left open in BRAINSTORM/nonab_frobenius_redei.md §3 (E2 channel); the only unchecked step is that the identity's solution stays Type I/II (coprimality) at generic such m², which fails only if (a²+b²) divides some X_i.

Listed as untried, but WINDMILL_REDUCTION §10 already does exactly this: a certificate (4uC−1)(4BC−1) = 4Cp+1 is the balanced Bhargava triple / 2×2×2 cube with Q₁=[m,2,m″] of disc −4tp (Lemma 10.1), the divisor hypercube embeds injectively in Cl(−4tp) (10.2, PROVED all p,t), and Prop 10.3 proves every mechanism factoring through form/cube classes and their S₃⋉(ℤ/2)³ symmetries sees m ≡ −1 (mod t) only via its genus shadow; Remark 10.4 identifies ray class groups mod t as the only class-type escape, which restates B2. No new composition law on (★) triples emerges.

Short proof attempt: for a prime q ∤ 2m, 'q ≡ −1 (mod m)' is equivalent to 'q is a primitive divisor of U_m(P,Q) for some (P,Q) with (D/q) = −1' (choose α/β of order m in the norm-1 torus of 𝔽_{q²}), so p-dependent Lucas sequences only restate the prime-certificate subcase of B2, while BHV guarantee a primitive divisor of U_m itself, never of 4Cp+1; tying them needs U_{4C}(P,Q) | 4Cp+1, a Thue-type coincidence of probability ~|α|^{−4C}. BRAINSTORM/y3_lucas_dickson_trace.md already records that Lucas ranks encode 4cd | h+1 but not the residue condition and that primitive divisors ≡ −1 (mod 4cd) divide U_{4cd}, not p+4c²d (B2), plus Prop G (Galois-descent collapse).

BRAINSTORM/z45_interlacing_stable.md already treats Lee–Yang/real stability/interlacing for exactly these divisor-sector polynomials, with exact computations at the hard primes and odd squares: MSS signings are all the same polynomial (gauge-removable), the class-extraction operator Π_{−1} destroys stability (e.g. at 2521 the only occupied level gives z²+z⁴; ∏(1+z_i) ↦ e₁+e₃), and the certificate-filtered real-rooted polynomial has a nonzero root iff the edge already exists. The item's first step (zeros of P_p(z)=Σ z^{u+B+C}) is weaker than this: P_p ≡ 0 exactly when R(p)=0, so its zero geometry cannot force existence; nothing beyond the memo.

Chen–Stein per se is not in the repo, but its ingredients (dependency neighbourhood mass b1/b2 ≈ Janson's Δ, Poisson zero law) are measured: BRAINSTORM/s9_janson_dependency.md finds word-level Δ/μ = 3.6 → 9.4 over 108k primes ≤ 3·10⁶ (so any Poisson/TV bound from word-level dependency graphs is vacuous, μ²/2Δ ≈ 1–2 ≪ log p), level-granularity hits are critical (0.44→0.97·log p); BM_CORRECTED_COUNT §3.2 and BOARD2_SLATE show R/2 is ≈ swap-Poisson at moderate M but the far lower tail is fatter than Poisson; (★) is overdispersed 1.5–1.6×. Also any over-ℤ Poisson upper bound is false by T1 (squares), so only a BM-corrected over-primes version is conceivable — already discussed there.

Computed the bound: for fixed u, F(B,C) = 4uBC − u − B − p has W ≈ max(4uXY, p) ≈ p at the certificate scale XY ≈ p/(4u), so Coppersmith's integer bivariate condition XY < W^{2/3} holds iff u ≳ p^{1/3}/4, i.e. the Lenstra/CHN 'divisors of p+u in a class mod 4u > N^{1/3} (resp. N^{1/4})' regime. BRAINSTORM/s3_lll_lenstra.md already did exactly this (Lenstra 1984; Coppersmith–Howgrave-Graham–Nagaraj 2008; certificate census: 58% Lenstra-regime, 28% Coppersmith-only, 14% below N^{1/4}) and notes the decisive point: the reduced-basis norms depend only on the lattice determinant, not on whether a root exists (Minkowski short vector always exists), so lattice shortness cannot serve as an existence criterion; results are upper bounds (≤ 11 per line).

Did not install PySR (Julia); cheap stand-in: computed the minimal Type II e-slice e_min(p) for all 9732 primes p≡1 (24) < 10⁶ (mean 5.7, 53% have e_min=3, max 63 at p=87481) and regressed log e_min on log p and one-hot p mod primes ≤ 43: log p explains R²=0.002, residues R²=0.51 (held-out 0.47). So e_min is 'congruence profile × lottery', exactly the hardness_law.md / ident_invariants.md picture (half the variance local data, rest near-Poisson noise); there is no size law in log p for symbolic regression to find, and any formula it returns would be a congruence-class covering (B1).

BRAINSTORM/z45_program_synthesis.md already ran the non-LLM version of this loop: enumerative synthesis over 924 policies scored by solved primes and charged operations on all 9,732 primes p≡1 (24) ≤ 10⁶, held-out on 73,155 primes in (10⁶,10⁷]; the best policy (López line p+4..p+16, then forest parent scan) costs ≤ 1.118(log p)², but the factor-free parent-scan baseline already solves everything to 10⁷ with better tail, i.e. the search recovers a known line plus a moving-divisor fallback. An LLM proposer would only enlarge the policy space; the memo's selection result (no mechanism, cost ∝ (log p)² lottery) leaves no specific new hypothesis for FunSearch to test.

The requested theorem shape ('τ(N) ≥ q^A and no obstruction ⇒ divisors of N cover (ℤ/q)^×') is false for structure-only hypotheses: LONGSHOT_PIGEONHOLE §1.4–1.5 proves (Kneser-based Prop 1.4) the exact covering criterion and its sharpness — k prime factors all in one generating class need k ≍ |G| even though each generates G, so any guarantee from orders/counts alone is linear in φ(q), not log; only 'general-position' (dissociativity) information about where specific large primes fall mod q bridges log→linear, and Theorem 2.2 there shows transparent covers fail for a positive proportion of primes. The random-residue alternative (Erdős–Rényi, 3^k ≳ φ(e) log φ(e)) is the heuristic regime recorded in the same section, B2_ACROSS_FIELDS row 9 and BRAINSTORM/s6_divisor_pigeonhole.md, z31_zero_sum.md.

For the 10 (★)-failing primes 409…8813281 and 6 controls, scanned levels C ≤ 2000: levels with Ω(4Cp+1) ≥ D*((ℤ/4C)^×) occur only at tiny C (1–3 levels per prime, C ≤ 6 except one C = 26), never at C ~ (log p)^A since D* grows like φ-scale while Ω(4Cp+1) ≤ log₂ N. At every failing prime these 'many-factor' levels exist but the factor classes generate a proper subgroup missing −1 (e.g. 577, C=2: Ω=6, all factors ≡ 3 mod 8; 712321, C=26: Ω=8=D*, subgroup of index 2 in φ=48), while at controls the subgroup contains −1 — i.e. failure is the genus/subgroup obstruction of LONGSHOT_PIGEONHOLE Lemma 1.2 / Prop 1.4, and smoothness with any count-type hypothesis is not the operative quantity.

BRAINSTORM/tech_smooth_level.md §3(b) already answers the first step: BFI/Zhang-type level beyond 1/2 only raises the admissible modulus range N^{1/2}→N^{1/2+ϖ}, i.e. the log-scale level λ of the CRT majorant, which changes the constant c but not the exponent in E(N) ≪ N exp(−c(log N)^{3/4}) because 3/4 is a structural mass/dimension cap ((D)24, EXCEPTIONAL_KARY3 Thm 4.1; (D)22 for prime-only majorants, (D)19 for large sieves); beating it needs growing-order correlation input TC_θ ((D)21), not level of distribution. The Titchmarsh-divisor average itself is LORENZINI_W Prop 6.1 / bsG_large_sieve_rate.md (PROVED relative to Linnik/Halberstam/BFI); Drappeau–Topacogullari uniformity in the residue modulus would likewise only move constants.

FRONTIER §3 (PARITY_AUDIT Remark 3.1) already rules this out as Assessment: Type II/bilinear fixed-modulus savings (Blomer–Pascadi, KMS, Bourgain–Garaev) would need a saving p^{1−o(1)} on unit coefficients, since on the modular hyperbola xy ≡ 1 (mod 4p) the certificate class condition x ≡ y ≡ −1 (mod 4C) has a height-dependent modulus C = (xy−1)/(4p); and in the (c,d)-expansion the Kloosterman moduli 4cd vary with the summation variables, so the (c,d)-average is not a KMS form (KMS needs one fixed prime modulus with the bilinear variables free). gon_incidence_kloosterman.md (c1) shows the mod-p (Weil/KMS) step is idle: all content is the moving-modulus divisibility with O(1) expectation per box.

Did the proposed rewrite: with d+1 = 4Ck, 4C ≡ k⁻¹ (mod d), so d | 4Cp+1 ⟺ d | p+k; the C-summed count becomes #{(k,C): (4Ck−1) | p+k}, i.e. p in the class −k mod d = 4Ck−1 — exactly PARITY_AUDIT Lemma 2.1's trial form R(p) = Σ_{(u,C)∈𝓡} 1[(4uC−1) | p+u], |𝓡| ≍ p log p events at one p. So 'τ in APs to large moduli averaged over C at fixed p' is a sum over moduli whose residue class (−k) is tied to the modulus, not a level-of-distribution statement with an averaged integer variable (B6; SINGLE_P_COUNT §6 'one level per prime', FRONTIER §3 Remark 3.1); BRAINSTORM/z39_gl3_shifted_divisor.md already identifies R as a boundary-truncated, additively shifted d₃.

The hyperbola/divisor form (tu−1)(tv−1) = tn+1 is the definition used throughout the I3 lane; LOWERTAIL_DEEP_FABLE §§4–7 and I3_DEEP_ASTRA already give the averaged main term ½log²n + O(log n) (all-integer density), the 112-zero census to 10⁹, the Vaughan-type exceptional bound and its optimality cap (EXSET_I3), and — the 'Kloosterman refinement' step itself — I3_DEEP_ASTRA §2 writes each balanced box count as Σ[1/m + (1/m)Σ_h e(h(n+u)/m)] with m = tu−1 and proves (Obs 2.1) that infinitely many boxes are empty, so the nonzero frequencies cancel the main term exactly and per-box dispersion/Kloosterman bounds cannot give positivity. Same tied-modulus obstruction as ES (FRONTIER §3 Remark 3.1).

Compared the per-level hit rate P(−1 ∈ divisor classes of N = 4Cp+1 mod 4C) for ~50k squarefree (p,C) (p ≡ 1 (4) in [10⁶, 1.2·10⁶], C ∈ {1,2,3,5,6,7,10,15}), grouped by k = ω(N), with exact-sampled random subset-product models: iid uniform units (A) badly overpredicts (k=1 gives 0 empirically: N ≡ 1 forces the product constraint), while the product-≡1-conditioned model (B) is right to within a factor ≈ 1.5–2 (e.g. C=7: emp .034/.14/.35/.67 vs B .086/.23/.45/.70 for k=2..5), with residual bias from small primes (3, 5, 7) whose classes are fixed. This is the pre-cutoff regime the item predicts and reproduces the repo's lottery picture (prob_lottery_model, s9_janson_dependency level-Poisson, LONGSHOT §1.5 random regime); no structure beyond it.

Short proof attempt: R(p) > 0 ⟺ the shell S = {(u,B,C) ∈ ℝ³_{>0} : p ≤ 4uBC − u − B < p+1} contains a lattice point (integer values), but S is not convex — it is a thin shell around the non-ruled cubic surface f = p, with normal thickness 1/|∇f| where |∇f| ≥ 4·max(BC,uC,uB) ≳ 4(p/4)^{2/3} (AM–GM: the three products multiply to (uBC)² ≈ (p/4)²), and its C-chords at fixed (u,B) have length 1/(4uB) ≤ 1/4. Hence every convex piece of S is automatically extremely thin (lattice width far below the flatness constant ω(3)) for every p, ES-true or not, so 'failure ⇒ all pieces flat' carries no information; in the 2-D (u,B) slices at fixed C the certificate set is the hyperbola (4uC−1)(4BC−1) = 4Cp+1 (measure zero), same conclusion.

Did the ω ≤ 3 classification by hand (PROVED, elementary): since N = 4Cp+1 ≡ 1 (mod m=4C), d ≡ −1 ⟺ N/d ≡ −1, so one may take d with ≤ ⌊Ω/2⌋ prime factors; hence for squarefree N with ω(N) ≤ 3 the character sum Σ_χ χ(−1)∏(1+χ(q)) vanishes iff no prime factor q ≡ −1 (mod 4C) (ω = 1: always vanishes; ω = 2: iff q₁ ≢ −1), and for ω = 4, 5 iff no prime or pair-product ≡ −1. The vanishing set is thus a union of 'no small subproduct hits −1' conditions — a restatement of the subset-product covering problem with no new forcing (cf. LONGSHOT_PIGEONHOLE §1.4 and EXACT_FORMULA's character expansion). Since ω(4Cp+1) is typically ~log log p, most levels are in this ω ≤ 3–5 regime, where failure just means no prime (or pair) factor lies in −1 mod 4C.

Computed doubling K = |Q·Q|/|Q| of the ratio sets Q = {ab⁻¹ mod 4C : ab | 4Cp+1} for C ≤ 200 at (★)-failing primes 409, 577, 8813281 and controls 433, 8813329: K is always small (mean ≈ 1.7, max ≤ 4.6) — automatically, since Q is the image of a k-dimensional GAP (K ≤ 3^ω) — and the statistics do not separate failing from control primes. The proposed reduction '−1 ∈ Q ⟺ −1 ∈ H' fails concretely: at 5–7 levels per prime with K ≤ 1.5 one has −1 ∈ ⟨Q⟩ but −1 ∉ Q; PFR's 'covered by few cosets of H' never forces Q ⊇ H, so it cannot locate a prescribed element (same covering-vs-structure gap as LONGSHOT_PIGEONHOLE Prop 1.4).

Formalised the hypergraph: vertices = (level C, class mod 4C of a prime factor of 4Cp+1); a certificate is a hyperedge = a multiset of classes at ONE level whose subproduct is −1. Edges never cross levels, so the hypergraph is a disjoint union of per-level components, codegrees across levels are 0, and the number of avoiding patterns factorises exactly as ∏_C #(avoiding patterns at C) — the container lemma adds nothing beyond the product/Poisson count. All cross-level dependence is through p itself (which patterns are realised by one p), i.e. the CRT/sieve step of mapping patterns to primes, which is exactly the architecture capped at exponent 3/4 by (D)24 (EXCEPTIONAL_KARY3 Thm 4.1, 'arbitrary moduli') and at level-Janson μ²/2Δ ≈ 1–2 by s9_janson_dependency.
